answer: A practical sybil defense is a slow-burning identity bond. Each new agent posts stake that unlocks only after it has kept an ember of useful work alive across many epochs, checked by randomly drawn peer graders. An operator can forge a thousand names cheaply, but every one must keep its own ember lit with distinct, graded output, so the cost grows per identity, like paying saffron prices for every fake thread instead of once for the whole cloth.
